# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}

    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>

    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType

    separator : String

    getRegex() : Pattern
}

}

    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String

    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode

}

    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy

}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper

TreeNode --|> BaseNode

TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children

    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a modified copy of this builder with a new prefix regex and minimum level, supporting fluent customization without mutating the original.
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke copySelf to produce an independent clone.
  2. On the clone, set prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex and minLevel = newMinLevel.
  3. Return the clone.
Related Features: writes PatternBuilder.prefixRegex and minLevel on the returned clone.
Related Classes: PatternBuilder.
Input: newPrefixRegex (String) - the new prefix regex; newMinLevel (int) - the new minimum allowed level.
Output: PatternBuilder - a new builder with the updated configuration.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is a syntactically valid regex fragment; newMinLevel is a positive integer.
Post-condition: the original builder is unchanged; the returned builder carries the new values.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the current builder configuration, throwing an exception if mandatory fields are missing or inconsistent.
Algorithm:
  1. Check that numberType, prefixRegex, and separator are non-null.
  2. Check that minLevel and maxLevel are positive and minLevel <= maxLevel.
  3. If any check fails, throw an IllegalStateException with a descriptive message.
Related Features: reads PatternBuilder fields: numberType, minLevel, maxLevel, prefixRegex, separator.
Related Classes: PatternBuilder.
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: the builder is verified consistent, or an exception is raised.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Returns a deep copy of this PatternBuilder so that further modifications do not affect the original configuration.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder instance.
  2. Copy numberType, minLevel, maxLevel, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex from this builder.
  3. Return the new builder.
Related Features: reads PatternBuilder fields: numberType, minLevel, maxLevel, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex.
Related Classes: PatternBuilder.
Input: none.
Output: PatternBuilder - a new builder with the same configuration.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: the returned builder is independent of this builder's mutable state.

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenation of this node's own content with the content of all its descendants, in traversal order, without inserting extra separators.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize result with this.content.
  2. For each child in children, recursively append child.getFullContent().
  3. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.content and TreeNode.children.
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: none.
Output: String - the full content of the subtree rooted at this node.
Pre-condition: tree structure is consistent (no cycles).
Post-condition: returned string preserves the traversal order of nodes.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Establishes a parent-child link by appending the supplied child node to this node's children list and setting the child's parent reference.
Algorithm:
  1. Append child to this.children.
  2. Set child.parent = this.
Related Features: writes TreeNode.children and TreeNode.parent.
Related Classes: TreeNode.
Input: child (TreeNode) - the node to attach.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: child is non-null and not already a child of another node (or reparenting is acceptable).
Post-condition: child appears in this.children and child.parent references this node.

TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Collapses all children into the current node by concatenating each child's full content into this node's content and clearing the children list.
Algorithm:
  1. For each child in children, append child.getFullContent() to this.content using BaseNode.concatNode semantics.
  2. Clear this.children.
  3. Optionally null out child.parent references for clarity.
Related Features: writes BaseNode.content and TreeNode.children.
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: tree structure is consistent.
Post-condition: this node's content includes all descendant content in traversal order and this.children is empty.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

LevelPattern::getRegex

Related Features: reads LevelPattern.regexText, separator; uses helper patterns if needed.

Input: none.
Output: Pattern - a compiled regular expression ready for matching.
Pre-condition: regexText is non-null and a valid regex fragment.
Post-condition: the returned Pattern can be used repeatedly for matching heading candidates.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Produces a human-readable textual representation of the outline tree using one line per node in the form "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>".
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize a StringBuilder.
  2. Invoke exportTreeInternal on the root with an empty prefix and isRoot=true.
  3. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.levelSeq and title.
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: tree (TreeNode) - the outline tree root.
Output: String - deterministic multi-line tree representation.
Pre-condition: tree is non-null.
Post-condition: the output contains one line per node and is stable across runs for the same tree.

TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursive helper that appends a single node's textual line and recursively appends its children, using a prefix to indicate tree structure.
Algorithm:
  1. Build the current line in the form "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>" and append it.
  2. For each child, compute the new prefix and recurse with isLast indicating whether it is the final child.
  3. Concatenate results in child order.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.levelSeq, title, children.
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: node (TreeNode) - the current subtree root; prefix (String) - accumulated indentation prefix; isLast (boolean) - whether this node is the last sibling; isRoot (boolean) - whether this is the synthetic root.
Output: String - concatenated tree representation including this subtree.
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: returned string reflects a stable traversal-order rendering.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into a map (EMap) suitable for JSON serialization, using the canonical field names title, level_seq, level_text, content, and children.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an empty EMap.
  2. Put "title" -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq" -> a list representation of node.levelSeq (sequence of integers).
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content" -> node.content.
  6. Recursively convert each child via nodeToDict and put the resulting list under "children".
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.title, levelSeq, levelText, content, and TreeNode.children.
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode, EMap.
Input: node (TreeNode) - the node to convert.
Output: EMap - map with the canonical keys for JSON export.
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: map contains exactly the five canonical keys for every node.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Serializes the outline tree to JSON and writes the result to a file at the given path.
Algorithm:
  1. Call exportToJson(tree) to obtain the JSON string.
  2. Open the file at filePath for writing (create parent directories if needed).
  3. Write the JSON string using UTF-8 encoding and close the file.
Related Features: invokes TreeExporter.exportToJson; uses Path.
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode, Path.
Input: tree (TreeNode) - the outline tree root; filePath (Path) - destination file path.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: filePath is writable; tree is non-null.
Post-condition: the file at filePath contains the pretty-printed JSON representation of the tree.

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary: Returns the prefix of a level sequence with the last element removed, i.e., the parent sequence candidate.
Algorithm:
  1. If levelSeq has fewer than two elements, return an empty list.
  2. Otherwise, return a new list containing all elements except the last.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.levelSeq.
Related Classes: BaseNode, EIntegerObject.
Input: levelSeq (List<EIntegerObject>) - the sequence whose prefix is needed.
Output: List<EIntegerObject> - the prefix sequence (empty if input is empty or has one element).
Pre-condition: levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition: returned list has size max(levelSeq.size() - 1, 0).

TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary: Indicates whether the given BaseNode corresponds to the synthetic root of the outline tree.
Algorithm:
  1. Return true if levelSeq is empty (and optionally title equals "ROOT").
  2. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.levelSeq, title.
Related Classes: BaseNode, TreeNode.
Input: node (BaseNode) - the node to test.
Output: boolean - true if the node is the synthetic root.
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: result is deterministic.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary: Returns the last integer value of a level sequence, which represents the most specific sublevel of a heading.
Algorithm:
  1. If levelSeq is empty, return 0 (indicating the synthetic root).
  2. Otherwise, return the integer value of the last element.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.levelSeq.
Related Classes: BaseNode, EIntegerObject.
Input: levelSeq (List<EIntegerObject>) - a comparable level sequence.
Output: int - the last level value (0 for root).
Pre-condition: levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition: result is the last element's integer value or 0.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Internal helper that performs the actual attachment of a chain node under its nearest valid ancestor, applying the auto-prune pending-queue rules.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq is a prefix of the new node's levelSeq; if none, fall back to the root.
  2. If the new node is an immediate valid next node relative to the current branch tip, call addNodeAndUpdateBranch to attach it.
  3. Otherwise, enqueue the node into a pending queue.
  4. If a later immediate node is found, dequeue and merge all pending nodes before it into the current node's content in arrival order.
  5. When the pending queue size reaches 3, invoke isAllNotImmNodesSiblings; if they form an immediate sibling sequence, attach them to the tree in order; otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the current node's content.
  6. After all input nodes are processed, drain any remaining pending nodes by merging their content into the current node.
Related Features: uses ChainNode fields (levelSeq, title, content, levelText), and TreeNode.addChild for attachment.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: node (ChainNode) - candidate node to attach; currentBranch (List<TreeNode>) - current valid branch; currentNodeRef (node) - mutable reference to the currently focused node used for merging pending content.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: currentBranch and currentNodeRef are initialized; the internal pending queue is available.
Post-condition: the node is either attached to the tree or merged into the current node's content; the pending queue state is updated.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches a chain node to the document tree under the auto-prune strategy, updating the current branch (the latest valid path from root to the most recently attached node) so that subsequent nodes can find the correct insertion point.
Algorithm:
  1. If currentBranch is empty or contains only the root, attach the node as a child of the root and append it to currentBranch.
  2. Otherwise, locate the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq is a prefix of the new node's levelSeq.
  3. Call addNodeToTree to attach the new node under that ancestor and refresh currentBranch so it ends at the new node.
  4. Handle pending nodes according to the auto-prune rules (see addNodeToTree).
Related Features: uses BaseNode.levelSeq for prefix comparison and TreeNode.addChild for attachment; relies on the maintained currentBranch list.
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy.

Output: void - the operation mutates the tree and currentBranch in place.

Post-condition: currentBranch is updated to represent the new root-to-newNode path; node is attached as a child of its correct ancestor.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds the full document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the auto-prune tolerant strategy that recovers from irregular level jumps.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize a synthetic root TreeNode with empty levelSeq and title "ROOT".
  2. Set currentBranch to [root] and currentNodeRef to root.
  3. For each chain node in order:
     a. Try to attach it as an immediate next node via addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
     b. If not immediate, recover by moving back along currentBranch to the nearest ancestor whose levelSeq is a prefix of the new node's levelSeq.
     c. If such an ancestor exists, attach the node under it; otherwise treat it as a child of root.
  4. After processing all nodes, return the root.
Related Features: consumes BaseNode fields (levelSeq, title, content) and constructs TreeNode objects via createTreeNode.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode, TreeBuildingStrategy.
Input: chain (List<ChainNode>) - the ordered list of parsed heading nodes produced by ChainParser.
Output: TreeNode - the synthetic root of the constructed outline tree.
Pre-condition: chain is non-null; each ChainNode has a non-empty levelSeq.
Post-condition: the returned TreeNode has a root titled "ROOT" with all chain nodes attached respecting the auto-prune tolerant rules.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Wraps a ChainNode into a fresh TreeNode, copying its title, level sequence, level text, and content while leaving children empty and parent null.
Algorithm:
  1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy title, levelSeq (List<int>), levelText, and content from the supplied ChainNode.
  3. Leave children as an empty list and parent as null.
  4. Return the new TreeNode.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.content, levelSeq, levelText, title.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: chainnode (ChainNode) - the parsed heading to wrap.
Output: TreeNode - a freshly created tree node detached from any parent.
Pre-condition: chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition: returned TreeNode has no parent and no children but carries all data fields from chainnode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Inspects the pending queue and determines whether all queued nodes form an immediate sibling sequence; if so they are attached to the tree in order, otherwise the oldest pending node is merged into the current node's content.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate the pending queue and, using isImmNext, verify that every consecutive pair of pending nodes is an immediate sibling.
  2. If all pending nodes satisfy this sibling relation, dequeue each in order and attach it to the appropriate parent in the tree, updating the current branch.
  3. Otherwise, pop the oldest pending node and call BaseNode.concatNode to merge its content into the current node's content.
Related Features: uses BaseNode.concatNode and BaseNode.levelSeq for sibling comparison.
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode.
Input: queue (Deque) - the pending node queue pending nodes that were not immediate successors.
Output: void - the queue and tree are mutated accordingly.
Pre-condition: queue size has reached the configured threshold (3).
Post-condition: the queue either becomes empty after attachment or has its oldest node removed and merged.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Internal helper that performs the actual attachment of a chain node under its nearest valid ancestor, applying the auto-prune pending-queue rules.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq is a prefix of the new node's levelSeq; if none, fall back to the root.
  2. If the new node is an immediate valid next node relative to the current branch tip, call addNodeAndUpdateBranch to attach it.
  3. Otherwise, enqueue the node into a pending queue.
  4. If a later immediate node is found, dequeue and merge all pending nodes before it into the current node's content in arrival order.
  5. When the pending queue size reaches 3, invoke isAllNotImmNodesSiblings; if they form an immediate sibling sequence, attach them to the tree in order; otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into the current node's content.
  6. After all input nodes are processed, drain any remaining pending nodes by merging their content into the current node.
Related Features: uses ChainNode fields (levelSeq, title, content, levelText), and TreeNode.addChild for attachment.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: node (ChainNode) - candidate node to attach; currentBranch (List<TreeNode>) - current valid branch; currentNodeRef (node) - mutable reference to the currently focused node used for merging pending content.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: currentBranch and currentNodeRef are initialized; the internal pending queue is available.
Post-condition: the node is either attached to the tree or merged into the current node's content; the pending queue state is updated.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches a chain node to the document tree under the auto-prune strategy, updating the current branch (the latest valid path from root to the most recently attached node) so that subsequent nodes can find the correct insertion point.
Algorithm:
  1. If currentBranch is empty or contains only the root, attach the node as a child of the root and append it to currentBranch.
  2. Otherwise, locate the nearest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq is a prefix of the new node's levelSeq.
  3. Call addNodeToTree to attach the new node under that ancestor and refresh currentBranch so it ends at the new node.
  4. Handle pending nodes according to the auto-prune rules (see addNodeToTree).
Related Features: uses BaseNode.levelSeq for prefix comparison and TreeNode.addChild for attachment; relies on the maintained currentBranch list.
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy.
Input: node (ChainNode) - the parsed heading node to attach; currentBranch (List<TreeNode>) - the current root-to-leaf path being maintained.
Output: void - the operation mutates the tree and currentBranch in place.
Pre-condition: node is a valid ChainNode whose levelSeq is non-empty; currentBranch is non-null and contains at least the root if not empty.
Post-condition: currentBranch is updated to represent the new root-to-newNode path; node is attached as a child of its correct ancestor.

If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Wraps a ChainNode into a fresh TreeNode for strict construction, copying its title, level sequence, level text, and content.
Algorithm:
  1. Allocate a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from the ChainNode.
  3. Leave children empty and parent null.
  4. Return the new TreeNode.
Related Features: reads BaseNode.content, levelSeq, levelText, title.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: chainnode (ChainNode) - the parsed heading to wrap.
Output: TreeNode - a freshly created tree node detached from any parent.
Pre-condition: chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition: returned TreeNode has no parent and no children but carries all data fields from chainnode.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Determines whether a given level sequence is the immediate child of another sequence, i.e., parentSeq equals the prefix of childSeq with exactly one extra trailing level.
Algorithm:
  1. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  2. For each index i in [0, parentSeq.size()), if parentSeq[i] != childSeq[i], return false.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: consumes BaseNode.levelSeq (represented as List<EIntegerObject> here).
Related Classes: BaseNode, EIntegerObject.
Input: parentSeq (List<EIntegerObject>) - candidate parent sequence; childSeq (List<EIntegerObject>) - candidate child sequence.
Output: boolean - true if childSeq extends parentSeq by exactly one level, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: both lists are non-null.
Post-condition: result is deterministic for any pair of inputs.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a document outline tree from a list of chain nodes using the strict strategy that rejects chains not rooted at the synthetic root.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a synthetic root TreeNode with empty levelSeq and title "ROOT".
  2. Iterate each ChainNode in order:
     a. If the node's levelSeq length is 1 and equals root + 1, attach it directly under root.
     b. Otherwise, locate the deepest existing ancestor whose levelSeq is the immediate prefix of the node's levelSeq using isChild.
     c. If no such ancestor exists, throw an exception (strict construction rejects irregular jumps).
     d. Attach the node under that ancestor via addChild.
  3. Return the root.
Related Features: uses BaseNode.levelSeq and TreeNode.addChild.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode.
Input: chain (List<ChainNode>) - the ordered list of parsed heading nodes.
Output: TreeNode - the synthetic root of the constructed tree.
Pre-condition: chain is non-null and each ChainNode has a non-empty levelSeq.
Post-condition: the tree strictly mirrors the level-sequence parent-child relation; an exception is raised if the chain is malformed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that constructs a ChainNode with the supplied parsed heading fields.
Algorithm:
  1. Allocate a new ChainNode.
  2. Set levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority from the parameters.
  3. Return the new ChainNode.
Related Features: sets BaseNode.content, levelSeq, levelText, title and ChainNode.patternPriority.
Related Classes: ChainNode, BaseNode.
Input: levelSeq (List<int>) - comparable level sequence; title (String) - heading title; content (String) - initial content; levelText (String) - original heading numbering text; patternPriority (int) - priority of the matched pattern.
Output: ChainNode - a freshly constructed chain node.
Pre-condition: all parameters are non-null where applicable.
Post-condition: a detached ChainNode carrying all supplied fields is returned.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Attempts to recognize a single text line as a heading by iterating through configured LevelPatterns in priority order and returning the first valid match as a ChainNode.
Algorithm:
  1. For each LevelPattern in patterns (in order):
     a. Match the line against the pattern's regex.
  2. If a match is found, call convertMatchedText on the matched numbering text to produce a level sequence of EIntegerObject values.
  3. Validate that the resulting sequence lies within [minLevel, maxLevel] for each element.
  4. If valid, build and return a ChainNode via createChainNode with the captured title, content, levelText, and patternPriority.
  5. If no pattern yields a valid heading, return null (the line will be treated as content).
Related Features: iterates ChainParser.patterns and invokes LevelPattern.convertMatchedText and getRegex.
Related Classes: LevelPattern, ParserHelper, ChainNode, BaseNode, EIntegerObject.
Input: line (String) - a single line of source text.
Output: ChainNode - the recognized heading, or null if the line is not a heading.
Pre-condition: patterns list has been initialized; helper utilities are available.
Post-condition: returned ChainNode (if any) has a non-empty levelSeq within the pattern's level bounds.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses an entire structured text document into an ordered list of ChainNodes, recognizing heading lines and preserving non-heading lines as content attached to the current section.
Algorithm:
  1. Maintain a "current" ChainNode that starts as a synthetic root with title "ROOT" and empty levelSeq.
  2. For each non-empty line in the input text:
     a. Call detectLevel.
     b. If a heading is returned, append the current node's accumulated content to the chain via createChainNode, then make the new heading the current node.
     c. Otherwise, append the line to the current node's content.
  3. After the loop, append the final current node to the chain.
  4. Return the chain.
Related Features: reads ChainParser.patterns; uses ChainNode fields; consumes BaseNode.content/title/levelSeq.
Related Classes: LevelPattern, ChainNode, BaseNode.
Input: text (String) - the full source document, separated by line breaks.
Output: List<ChainNode> - ordered chain of heading nodes, each carrying the content that follows it up to the next heading.
Pre-condition: text is non-null; patterns are configured.
Post-condition: the returned chain is ordered, each node has a non-empty levelSeq (except possibly a synthetic root), and content fields are populated in traversal order without extra separators.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuilder::buildTree
Summary: Delegates tree construction to the configured TreeBuildingStrategy, providing a uniform entry point regardless of strict or auto-prune behavior.
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke strategy.buildTree(chain).
  2. Return the resulting TreeNode.
Related Features: reads TreeBuilder.strategy.
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy, TreeNode, ChainNode.
Input: chain (List<ChainNode>) - the ordered chain of parsed headings.
Output: TreeNode - the constructed outline tree.
Pre-condition: strategy has been initialized.
Post-condition: the returned tree reflects the rules of the configured strategy.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

class AutoPruneStrategy {

}

}

    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String

A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
